correctness.rationale: For n>=7, the six eligible seed-pair orbit types are same-rail separations 1,2,3 and opposite-rail separations 0,1,2 (distance-at-most-three lemma of Girish–Somasundaram). Directly checked each initial rail-observation set, its q=1,2,2,0,1,1 post-domination fills, and the L=4,5,6,3,4,5 complete rung intervals. Each subsequent simultaneous round expands both interval ends, hence t=1+q+ceil((n-L)/2). Type counts (2n each same 1/2/3; n,2n,2n opposite 0/1/2) yield precisely 11n and 3n/8n fastest/slowest odd, 9n/2n even. Independent direct simulation of ALL unordered pairs for n=7..18 reproduced every value, including nonqualifying pairs; it does not prove arbitrary n.
residual_risks: Time convention includes the initial N[S] round and requires simultaneous forces. Six-base proof uses coordinate collisions only controlled for n>=7; finite simulation is corroboration.
